cards.front: List the five values required to build the main box and whiskers of a box plot.
cards.back: Smallest non-outlier valueLower Quartile ($Q_1$)MedianUpper Quartile ($Q_3$)Largest non-outlier value

cards.front: To find the lower quartile ($Q_1$) of an ordered data set, calculate the [ ___ ] of the lower half of the data.
cards.back: To find the lower quartile ($Q_1$) of an ordered data set, calculate the median of the lower half of the data.

cards.front: To find the lower quartile ($Q_1$) of an ordered data set, calculate the median of the [ ___ ] of the data.
cards.back: To find the lower quartile ($Q_1$) of an ordered data set, calculate the median of the lower half of the data.

cards.front: When finding quartiles for an odd number of data values, how is the overall median treated?
cards.back: It is excluded from both the lower and upper halves of the data.

cards.front: State the formula for calculating the Interquartile Range (IQR).
What does a smaller IQR indicate about the data distribution?
cards.back: The middle 50% of the data are more tightly clustered (greater consistency).

cards.front: State the formula for the lower fence used to identify outliers.
cards.back: $$$Q_1 - 1.5 \times IQR$$

cards.front: State the formula for the upper fence used to identify outliers.
cards.back: $$$Q_3 + 1.5 \times IQR$$

cards.front: A value is considered an outlier if it is [ ___ ] the lower fence or greater than the upper fence.
cards.back: A value is considered an outlier if it is smaller than the lower fence or greater than the upper fence.

cards.front: A value is considered an outlier if it is smaller than the lower fence or [ ___ ] the upper fence.
cards.back: A value is considered an outlier if it is smaller than the lower fence or greater than the upper fence.

cards.front: If a data value is exactly equal to the upper fence, is it classified as an outlier?
cards.back: No; it must be strictly greater than the fence.

cards.front: Where must the whiskers of a box plot end if outliers are present?
cards.back: At the smallest and largest non-outlier values.

cards.front: How are outliers represented on a box plot?
cards.back: Separately using crosses.

cards.front: In a box plot, the box itself represents the middle [ ___ ] of the data, while each whisker represents approximately 25%.
cards.back: In a box plot, the box itself represents the middle 50% of the data, while each whisker represents approximately 25%.

cards.front: In a box plot, the box itself represents the middle 50% of the data, while each whisker represents approximately [ ___ ].
cards.back: In a box plot, the box itself represents the middle 50% of the data, while each whisker represents approximately 25%.

cards.front: In a box plot, which specific feature represents the time by which 75% of a group has finished a task?
cards.back: The Upper Quartile ($Q_3$).

cards.front: When comparing two distributions, which statistic should be used to compare average location?
cards.back: The median.

cards.front: When comparing two distributions, which statistic should be used to compare consistency (spread of the middle 50%)?
cards.back: The Interquartile Range (IQR).

cards.front: A box plot shows a median of 13 and an IQR of 8. Another shows a median of 15 and an IQR of 5. Which set is more consistent?
cards.back: The second set, because it has a lower IQR.

cards.front: Identify the median position in an ordered list of 11 values.
cards.back: The 6th value.

cards.front: When drawing a box plot, the [ ___ ] is drawn as a vertical line inside the box.
cards.back: When drawing a box plot, the median is drawn as a vertical line inside the box.

cards.front: When drawing a box plot, the median is drawn as a [ ___ ] inside the box.
cards.back: When drawing a box plot, the median is drawn as a vertical line inside the box.

cards.front: Why is the IQR often preferred over the range when discussing spread?
cards.back: The range is significantly affected by extreme values (outliers), whereas the IQR focuses on the central values.

cards.front: If $n=15$, which value is the median, and how many values are in the lower half?
cards.back: Median: 8th valueLower half: 7 values
